stories.headline: Cunha Leads, test3331 Comes Up Light
stories.deck: test2 beat test3331 49-40, Cunha's eight the top score.
stories.body:
Cunha settled it. Eight from the forward slot led test2's line, Isak six alongside him, and the back three of Ajayi, Giles and Hall returned six apiece. Six from Millar in midfield too. No blank anywhere on the sheet, and that spread is why the margin read nine.

test3331 had Scott top-scoring on seven and honest sixes from Ndoye, Thomas and White. The floor was the problem. Lewis-Potter's five and Cook's three at the bottom of the midfield gave nothing back, and there was no eight or nine anywhere to answer Cunha.

test3331 needed one man to go big and got a ceiling of seven. Six sixes for test2, one from every filled slot, made the difference no single haul could close.

stories.headline: Cherki Sharp, testf Falls Eleven Short
stories.deck: test4 beat testf 56 to 45, Cherki's eleven leading the way.
stories.body:
Cherki topped it with eleven for test4, Foden and Mbeumo both on eight behind him. Elanga six, Raya six from the clean sheet, Isidor a five to round the return. Six men, every one on the board.

testf never got there. Tarkowski led with eight, Tzolakis seven, Ballard six, and a back line doing more than the front. Evanilson and Rogers both blanked to fives, Barnes stranded on three.

The forwards were the wound. testf needed his attackers to answer Cherki and got twenty-two of his forty-five from two defenders and a keeper. Eleven short, and it points straight at the men up top.

stories.headline: Gibbs-White Tips test3 Over The Line
stories.deck: test3 beat test31 38-28, Gibbs-White's ten leading the way
stories.body:
Gibbs-White's ten fronted it for test3, and Calafiori's nine behind him made the margin safe. Wissa added six, Maguire four, Pickford three from the sticks, Gonzalo two. Thirty-eight, and never really threatened.

test31 had no answer in the same weight class. Thiaw's six was the top score and it topped out at that; Belloumi and Munoz five apiece, Bobb three, Barry and Buendía two each. Six men, twenty-eight, no single haul to build on.

That is the difference laid bare. test3 got a ten and a nine; test31's best pair barely cleared the number Calafiori managed alone.

stories.headline: Fernandes Twenty, test31121 Nowhere Near
stories.deck: 123 76 beat test31121 35, a 41-point rout led by B.Fernandes' 20.
stories.body:
B.Fernandes settled this on his own. Twenty points from midfield, double the next man on either side, and 123 were already clear before the rest filed in. Groß and Haaland matched at ten apiece, and a 76 was assembled without a single passenger.

test31121 topped out at six. Gabriel returned it from defence, Botman gave him five more from the same slot, but the ceiling was the problem: no man broke seven, four of six sat at five or under. A 35 needs a captain who hauls. He got none.

Horníček's seven and a clean sheet from Hume padded the gap. Ødegaard and Petrović both stopped at three, and against a 20-point midfielder there was nothing left to find. Forty-one is not a bad night's football lost, it is a mismatch of engines.

stories.headline: test1 Spread Loads, Pedro Left Wanting
stories.deck: test1 beats test211 48-40, six contributors to test211's top-heavy 40.
stories.body:
test1 got there by committee. Lavia and Palmer led the midfield with seven apiece, Calvert-Lewin, Egan and Saka all returned six, Semenyo five. No blank in the six, nothing under five, and 48 on the board.

test211 leaned on João Pedro's seven up top and got nothing else to match it. Castagne and Roefs returned six each, then the drop: Enciso and Gakpo five apiece, Fatawu four.

That Fatawu four is the number that hurts. test211 needed his forwards firing to keep pace and one of them managed four. Eight short.

stories.headline: Isidor Twenty-Six, Fulham Nil
stories.deck: Sunderland beat Fulham 1-0, Isidor's goal in twenty-six minutes the difference for test4
stories.body:
One goal decided it and Isidor had it, five points off twenty-six minutes for test4. A forward on the pitch barely a third of the match, gone before the hour, and the return dwarfs the men who saw it out.

The clean sheets stacked up either side. Roefs and Castagne kept it tight for test211, six apiece, Castagne off sixty-seven with the shutout intact. Reinildo and Hume held the line for 123, six each. Ballard did the same for testf, though N.Angulo blanked the clean sheet into two and Xhaka's three barely registers. Leno faced it at the other end, three saves for test3331, a losing keeper still on three.

Gonzalo played the ninety and returned nothing for test3, a forward's blank. E.Le Fée's shutout gives test4 three more on top of Isidor's five, a fine afternoon for one manager. King, Berge, Bobb: small change, two and two and three.

Across the head-to-heads it barely moves the settled ones. test4 sit 56 to 45 over testf, all but done. 123 tower 76 to 35 over test31121, the clean-sheet pair carrying it home.

stories.headline: Gibbs-White Alone Denies The Reds
stories.deck: Liverpool drew 2-2 with Nott'm Forest; Gibbs-White returned ten with a goal and an assist.
stories.body:
Two apiece, and Forest walk away with the ten-point man. Gibbs-White scored and set one up, ninety minutes, the full haul for test3. Ndoye backed him with a goal off sixty-five, six points, and N.Williams from the back added an assist for test4. Forest's rostered men did the damage.

Liverpool's midfield offered little. Wirtz got the assist and the booking, ninety and four points for test1. Szoboszlai ninety and blank at two for test31121, Gravenberch nineteen minutes and one for test1. Gakpo drew an assist off seventy for test211, five more, the faith intact.

Munoz scored and was booked, five for test31. Isak scored, six for test2, Isak's ninety worth every one of them. McAtee ninety and two for test2. Aina eighty-five, booked, nothing, a blank for test211.

Gibbs-White's ten stretches test3 to 38-28 over test31, all but done despite Munoz's return. test211's 40 sits behind test1's 48, Gakpo and Aina splitting.

stories.headline: Groß Profit In Seven-Goal Split
stories.deck: Chelsea beat Brighton 4-3, and 123's Groß leads the way with ten
stories.body:
Seven goals shared, four to Chelsea, and the fantasy ledger runs almost as long as the scoreline. Groß was the pick of it, a goal and an assist for ten points to 123, with Neto adding a goal and Lacroix a limp single from ninety.

João Pedro carried the load and the burden both, a goal and an assist undercut by an own goal, seven points to test211 that read better before the deduction. Palmer and Lavia struck for a goal apiece, seven each, test1 twice in profit on the same afternoon.

The Brighton back end offered nothing worth owning. De Cuyper and Verbruggen blanked at zero for test31, and Dunk's booking dragged test3 into the red at minus one. Kostoulas found an assist for five, Rogers likewise for testf.

stories.headline: Schade And Calvert-Lewin Shade The Points
stories.deck: Leeds and Brentford drew 1-1, both scorers rostered and returning six.
stories.body:
The one goal apiece came off two forwards this league owns. Schade struck for Brentford, six points to 123 across eighty-seven minutes. Calvert-Lewin answered for Leeds, six for test1 across the ninety.

Lewis-Potter fed one for test3331, five points and the game's best supporting return. Damsgaard held a clean sheet through sixty-eight, three for test211. Trafford kept four out for test2, three points, while Kelleher managed a single save at the other end.

Stach filled the ninety without a return, two for 123. Ajer went into the book for one, test3331's other man. Ampadu, Justin, Bogle full backs of the scoreboard variety, twos across the board. Aaronson lasted forty-five for a single point, Rodon thirty-three for the same. Jensen never left the bench for test3.

Schade's six does nothing to dent 123's 76-35 rout of test31121. test1's Calvert-Lewin keeps the pressure on in a tie test211 lead 48-40, all but sealed. test2's 49-40 over test3331 holds, Trafford and Lewis-Potter cancelling out on the same page.

stories.headline: Gakpo Stays, test211 Keeps The Faith
stories.deck: Liverpool keep Cody Gakpo, owned by test211, amid Barcola's arrival.
stories.body:
Iraola talked up his window and set Bradley Barcola for a debut, but the line that matters here: Cody Gakpo stays. test211 keeps a starter, not a squad piece cast into doubt by an incoming forward.

What the minutes look like with Barcola through the door is not said, so it is not written here. test211 holds an asset that was never sold. That is the whole of it for now.

stories.headline: test3 Banks a City Slicker
stories.deck: test3's Ndiaye joins Manchester City from Everton for up to £65m.
stories.body:
Ndiaye is test3's, and now he is City's too. The winger moves from Everton in a deal reported up to £65m, and the shirt change is the only fact that matters here.

What it does to test3's returns nobody yet knows. New club, new competition for minutes, no word on where he slots. test3 holds the asset and waits like everyone else.

stories.headline: 123 Banks a Big-Money Backline
stories.deck: Lacroix, one of the summer's twenty priciest signings, sits on 123's roster.
stories.body:
The BBC's ledger of the window's twenty biggest fees runs from Enzo Fernandez down to Maxence Lacroix. Only the last name matters here: Lacroix belongs to 123.

What the fee buys on the pitch is 123's problem to solve, and the wire says nothing of minutes or fitness. For now it is a name on a list and a name on a roster, and both read the same.

stories.headline: Fernandes Files A Full Report
stories.deck: B.Fernandes hauls three goals and an assist to headline the team of the week in a 3-5-3.
stories.body:
B.Fernandes is the man of the week and the argument is over before it starts: three goals and an assist from midfield, ninety minutes, nothing left on the table. A midfielder outscoring the forwards is the whole story, and 123 had him.

The back three picks itself on returns and clean sheets both. Calafiori kept his sheet and chipped in an assist, Tarkowski went one better and scored his, and that goal is what edges 123's Reinildo out of the frame despite a six that on another week walks in. The Dedić case is its own scandal below.

The middle is where this side is won. Cherki's two goals from midfield off eighty-one minutes is a forward's return in a playmaker's shirt, Gibbs-White and Groß both paired a goal with an assist, and Scott married a goal to a clean sheet from the engine room. Five across the park and every one of them returned twice over.

Up top Haaland's brace leads a front line that all pulled their weight: Mbeumo and João Pedro each took a goal and an assist. Three forwards, six combined returns, no passengers.

Unlucky is the wrong word for Dedić, who was benched by his own manager and still turned in an assist and a clean sheet, so spare the sympathy for someone who missed out entirely. The three at the back over a fourth defender is the only shape that fits this many attacking midfielders, and it fits like a glove.

captions.line: Three goals and an assist from midfield, and the rest of the eleven are playing for second.
A brace and the responsibility of leading the line, both discharged without fuss.
Two goals inside eighty-one minutes, a forward's haul stitched onto a midfielder's shirt.
A goal and an assist across the full ninety, the complete midfield afternoon.
A goal and an assist, and nobody in this front three carried more than his share better.
A goal and an assist, quietly doing exactly what a forward in this side is asked to.
A goal and a clean sheet from midfield in eighty-six, two jobs done at once.
A goal and an assist over ninety, ruthlessly efficient in the middle of the park.
A defender who scored his own goal, and that goal is why he is here.
An assist and a clean sheet from a man his own manager did not trust to start.
A clean sheet kept and an assist supplied, the defender who did both ends of the pitch.

stories.headline: Points Table Lies, Scoreboard Tells Truth
stories.deck: 123 and testf are the two best sides going, and the record hides both.
stories.body:
The table has test2 and test3 top on maximum points, and neither has done anything to argue with. But 6 points off 96 and 93 is honest, unspectacular work. Beating test3331 by 9 and test31 by 10 is a win banked, not a statement made. They are where they are because they scheduled it right.

The real ceiling sits at third and ninth. 123 put up a league-high 103 and buried test31121 by 41, and the table thanks them with 3 points. testf scored 94, more than three sides sitting above them, and has nothing. That is not football failing, that is the fixture list. test3331 and testf are the two zeros, but only one of them looks like a team going nowhere.

ranks.line: League-high 103 and a 41-point demolition; third is an insult the scoreboard will correct.
97 and an eight-point win over a live test211 side; quietly the most complete of the winners.
Top of the table, 96 scored, and yet you sense they beat a corpse in test3331.
Two from two on 93, but ten past test31 flatters a side that has not been tested.
97 and eleven clear of testf, but the schedule handed them the softest zero to beat.
94 in defeat by eight; unlucky in the draw, not outclassed in the football.
94 scored and bottom-but-one on nothing; the phantom zero is a scheduling crime, not a form guide.
83 and beaten by ten; the points are real but the score is thin.
79 and a 41-point hiding; the lowest ceiling in the league right now.
91 across two and still winless; competitive on the scoreboard, invisible on the table, going backwards either way.

stories.headline: Left Behind, Marked Present
stories.deck: Five benched players did their jobs while their managers watched from the wrong end of the lineup.
stories.body:
test31121 leads the parade twice over. Yalcouyé rewarded the bench with a goal in 73 minutes, and Gvardiol chipped in an assist across 74, both from the wrong side of the team sheet. One manager, two men delivering to nobody.

Dedić kept a clean sheet over the full 90 for test3331 and added an assist for good measure, the complete defensive shift wasted. Davis matched the goal on the other flank of the ledger, 90 minutes and a strike, left out by test4.

Diarra needed only 18 minutes to log an assist for test1, the shortest cameo on the list and no less pointed for it. Five men, five contributions, none of them counted.

stories.headline: Two Deals, No Rush, Raya Waits
stories.deck: A quiet gameweek 2 window: only two moves made across the league.
stories.body:
Two deals. That is the week. test4 swapped one for one, test31 and testf added a body apiece and closed the laptop. No churn, no bidding war, no man passed hand to hand. If gameweek 2 had a pulse it kept it well hidden.

testf was the only mover with a grievance to nurse. A second body brought in, a second round of nothing to show for it. Ninety-four scored and beaten by eleven; the reinforcement arrives into a squad that keeps blanking through no fault of the numbers.

David Raya. Signed in hope, dropped without ceremony, survives on the waiver wire. No claim has come. He waits, unclaimed, a goalkeeper nobody wants and nobody will bury.

test4 alone traded rather than hoarded, one out to make room for one in. Everyone else stood pat. Two deals is quiet, and calling it anything else would be inflation.

quiz.q: How many deals were struck in the gameweek 2 window?
Which manager was the only one to drop a player as well as add one?
Name the dropped goalkeeper still sitting unclaimed on the wire.
Which two managers added a player without dropping anyone?
How many points did testf score before losing by eleven?
